title: Why Linux is making a comeback on desktop

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Linux is making a comeback because open-source protocols finally outperform proprietary ones on the desktop.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Windows and macOS still dominate because of seamless hardware integration, driver support, and user-friendly interfaces.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Linux now has full Wayland support, better GPU acceleration, and distributions like Pop OS that rival Windows in polish.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: The real comeback is in security—Linux has fewer vulnerabilities, and its modular design prevents widespread breaches.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Linux is the future—secure, customizable, and built on principles that empower users, not lock them in.
